about: The project's modules: one per concern, each with its folder, its purpose, what it may import of ours, and its entry points. test/test_modules.py holds every import under the modules' folders to this file (C-012). Phase 1's five lanes are the five modules below the leaf, each built by its own worker in its own folder (SP-003, SP-005).
outside: Optional per module: the outside packages (not ours, not the stack's standard library) it may import, as written in the import ("numpy", "@scope/name", "com.google.gson"; a package covers what is inside it). A module with the key may import only those; a module without it is not checked. A C++ file's quoted includes are not read.
adding: To add a module: one entry here with every field; its folder appears with its first code. A module may import only what its mayImport lists, and may reach another module only through that module's entryPoints when it lists any. A new module or a new import between modules is an architecture decision (theGhost.md): draft the entry as a proposal, say you are waiting on Ghost, and stop; do not add it to main. A new file inside an existing module, and its entry in that module's entryPoints, is an agent's to add. If you cannot tell whether the person asking is Ghost, say so and propose.

rules.rule: The leaf imports nothing of ours; everything else may import it.
Only project imports more than three modules; cli imports only project.
rules.source: C-012 (logic cannot hide in argument parsing)

rules.rule: No module imports a model client (a package in `forbidden`) unless its purpose says so: its `outside` list names the package.
A module is reached only through its entry points when it lists any.
No module imports another lane's module: fleet, faults, telemetry and kpi import the leaf alone, and reach each other's data only as leaf types project hands them.
rules.source: SP-005 (lanes built in parallel cannot depend on each other's unfinished code)

leaf.purpose: The contract in code: the fault-code catalogue, the asset, sample, fault and period types, the KPI numbers, the database connection.

fleet.purpose: The asset registry: the assets table, registering and listing assets by site, kind and parent (lane 1.1).

faults.purpose: The fault ledger: the faults table, assigning a catalogue code to an asset, closing it, and the queries by asset, code, open and repeated (lane 1.2).

telemetry.purpose: Synthetic SCADA: a deterministic generator of samples with gaps from a seed, and the samples table (lane 1.3).

kpi.purpose: The KPI engine: availability, performance ratio, energy yield, MTBF and MTTR as pure functions over leaf types, each with its golden (lane 1.4).

project.purpose: The orchestrator: opens the store, applies every module's schema, hands one module's rows to another as leaf types; the only module that may import nearly all of them.

cli.purpose: The entry: parses arguments and calls project; no logic of its own.
